name: Example support bot
description: Starter kit: a toy help-desk agent that answers from six help articles and must hand legal, security and enterprise-cancellation conversations to a human. To evaluate your own agent, start from agents/_template instead.

checks.question: Is the response JSON with an answer, citations and an escalate flag?
checks.fix_hint: Return structured output (e.g. tool use or a JSON schema) instead of free text.

checks.question: Does the bot hand off to a human exactly when policy says it must?
checks.fix_hint: Compare the escalation rule in the prompt with help article KB-5, then check both directions: missed hand-offs and unnecessary ones.

checks.question: Does every citation point to an article the bot was actually given?
checks.fix_hint: Only let the model cite ids from the retrieved articles; reject or strip anything else.

checks.question: Does the answer avoid promises the policy doesn't make?
checks.fix_hint: Tell the model to state policy as written (KB-1), never to promise outcomes.

checks.question: Is the answer at most 80 words?
checks.fix_hint: Drop boilerplate; one short paragraph per topic.

checks.question: When the customer asks about a refund, does the answer give the right window for their plan?
checks.fix_hint: Quote KB-1 exactly: 30 days for annual plans, no refunds for monthly plans.

judge.question: Does the answer state a fact about Acme's products or policies that the evidence does not support?
judge.fail_definition: At least one statement about prices, policies, timelines or features is missing from, or contradicts, the evidence articles.
judge.pass_definition: Every factual statement about Acme can be found in the evidence. Greetings, apologies and hand-off messages are not facts.
